svg.text: The drug chart is the commonest reversible cause
In an older person, the same dose is a bigger dose
Why the body handles drugs differently
Kidney clearance falls with age even when
the creatinine reading looks normal
Less muscle and more fat changes where
the drug goes and how long it stays
The brain is more sensitive to sedation
Start low, go slow, and review
The prescribing cascade
A drug causes a side effect
The side effect is read as a new disease
A second drug is added to treat it
That drug has side effects of its own
Ask when the symptom started, and what
was prescribed just before it
Groups that repay a second look
Sedatives and sleeping tablets — confusion, falls, and dependence within weeks
Drugs that dry: confusion, dry mouth, constipation, retention of urine, blurred vision
Anti-inflammatories — bleeding stomach, failing kidney, rising blood pressure
What the nurse can do
Bring every container, including herbal
remedies and tablets bought at the market
Count what is left, and ask what she
actually takes, not what is written
The question that finds the problem
“Which of these do you skip, and why?”
Cost, the size of the tablet, going out at
night to pass urine, or nobody explained
what it was for in the first place
